title: datetime
summary: Create host datetime arrays from date vectors, text, calendar components, or explicit serial-date conversions.

gpu_support.notes: datetime values are host-side objects backed by serial date tensors; there is no GPU-resident datetime type.

description: `datetime` constructs host-side datetime objects from m-by-3 or m-by-6 date vectors, text, and the documented 3-, 6-, or 7-component forms. All eight integer classes are read from authoritative storage before RunMat crosses into its current floating serial-date representation. `ConvertFrom='datenum'` is implemented; other documented conversion epochs, time zones, locale and pivot-year options, and general nanosecond fidelity remain explicit gaps.
behaviors: `datetime()` with no arguments returns the current local date and time.

`datetime(dateVectors)` accepts m-by-3 and m-by-6 numeric matrices. `datetime(Y, M, D)`, `datetime(Y, M, D, H, MN, S)`, and `datetime(Y, M, D, H, MN, S, MS)` accept single, double, and all eight integer classes; scalar inputs expand to matching non-scalar component arrays.

Calendar components normalize by carrying into adjacent units. NaN components produce NaT and infinite components retain the corresponding infinite serial marker within the current host representation.
`datetime(text)` accepts string scalars, string arrays, and character vectors. Supported text includes common ISO-like forms, `dd-MMM-yyyy`, `now`, `today`, `tomorrow`, and `yesterday`.
`datetime(serials, 'ConvertFrom', 'datenum')` interprets numeric values as MATLAB serial date numbers.

A one-argument numeric value that is not an m-by-3 or m-by-6 date-vector matrix is interpreted as a raw serial date only when RunMat compatibility extensions are enabled. MATLAB-compatible mode requires the explicit `ConvertFrom` form.

Four- and five-component forms, logical numeric inputs, and gathering resident numeric arrays are compatibility-gated RunMat extensions. The resident gate is checked before provider access and the result is always a host datetime object.

Only `Format`, `InputFormat`, and `ConvertFrom='datenum'` are currently implemented. Other documented `ConvertFrom` values and the `Locale`, `PivotYear`, `TimeZone`, `Epoch`, and `TicksPerSecond` options report unsupported-input errors rather than silently approximating semantics.
The `Format` property controls text rendering. Assigning `t.Format = 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss'` updates how the object displays without changing the stored point in time.
Linear indexing `t(k)` is supported and returns datetime values.
Comparison operators and `plus`/`minus` day arithmetic are supported. Subtracting two datetime values returns numeric day deltas.
`now`, `today`, and `clock` expose current local time in MATLAB-compatible serial, datetime, and date-vector forms.
`datenum`, `datevec`, `datestr`, `weekday`, `eomday`, `etime`, and `isbetween` cover common legacy serial-date conversion, formatting, query, and interval operations.
`datetime + calendarDuration` and `datetime - calendarDuration` apply month-aware calendar arithmetic with end-of-month clamping.

`isbusday`, `holidays`, `busdays`, `days252bus`, `daysdif`, `fbusdate`, and `lbusdate` provide weekday plus market-holiday business-calendar compatibility for standard scripts. Custom weekend definitions and all Financial Toolbox option forms are not yet implemented.

faqs.question: What does the `Format` property change?
faqs.answer: Only the textual representation. The stored serial date number is unchanged, so comparisons and arithmetic still refer to the same instant.

faqs.question: How is subtraction interpreted?
faqs.answer: Subtracting one datetime from another returns a numeric delta measured in days. Subtracting a numeric value from a datetime shifts it backward by that many days.

faqs.question: Can I index datetime arrays?
faqs.answer: Yes. Linear `()` indexing is supported and preserves the datetime type.

faqs.question: Does `datetime` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No public resident datetime type is implemented. MATLAB-compatible mode rejects resident numeric constructor inputs before provider access; RunMat extension mode may gather them and still returns a host-side datetime object.

gpu_residency: No. RunMat represents `datetime` values as host-side objects with an internal serial-date tensor and a `Format` property. Resident numeric constructor input is compatibility-gated before provider access, and an enabled extension gathers to a CPU result.
gpu_behavior: `datetime` does not allocate GPU objects or invoke provider kernels. MATLAB-compatible mode rejects resident inputs before lookup; RunMat extension mode gathers before building the host object.
